question: As of September 18, 2026, will NASA have announced a specific-day launch date for SpaceX Crew-13?

calls.reasoning: Status quo is a window-only listing: NASA's Crew-13 page has read 'NET Late Sept. 2026' since its Sept 3 update, the Crew-13 blog's last post is Aug 29, and 10.7 of the 21 days from stand-down to deadline have passed with no specific day named. Reference class (crewed ISS missions on indefinite hold for a spacecraft hardware anomaly, specific day named within ~21 days) runs ~0.55, but every YES analog I found (Crew-6 ~3d, Crew-9 ~7d, Ax-4 ~11d) named its date inside 11 days, while the slow cases (Soyuz MS-22, Starliner OFT-2, 2019 Dragon anomaly) named none in days 11-21 — we have already survived the fast tail, which is a genuine negative update. Pushing up: Isaacman's public 2-4 week repair estimate puts the decision point at Sept 12-26; the fault is described as a component-level valve/NTO leak with no fleet-wide inspection announced; Crew-12's Dragon was recertified to 8 months from a Feb 14 docking (~Oct 14 limit), forcing schedule commitment; and the YES bar is low ('NET Oct. 8' qualifies, any credible source qualifies). Pushing down: NASA's habitual intermediate step when slipping across a month is another window ('NET October'), which is exactly NO; root cause is undisclosed; no NASA briefing or FRR is scheduled Sept 8-18 (searched, absent); and the Crew-12 limit is relievable via indirect handover, which this station already ran at reduced crew in early 2026. Markets: no Kalshi/Polymarket contract; Manifold's 0.18 on Ṁ178 prices physical liftoff by Sept 30, a different threshold/deadline/instrument, so it is corroboration that late-September is unlikely, not an anchor. Scenario weights (late-Sept launch 20% x 0.92; Oct 1-15 launch 45% x 0.55; late-Oct/Nov 25% x 0.15; extended stand-down 10% x 0.03) give ~0.47; the day-11 conditioning and the absent announcement calendar pull it to 0.40.
